title: What should an AI game remix carry forward besides source and credit?
author: biggdogg420
selftext:
I’m testing a handoff format for small browser-game remixes: enough context that another person or AI can continue the game without losing where it came from.

The current experiment keeps the source project, original credits, parent/remix lineage and a short AI brief together. In practice, a Pong remix made with Claude Code and two other playable prototypes built with Codex have made me think the hard part is preserving permissions and intent alongside code.

What would make this useful in your AI-assisted game workflow? I’m especially curious whether you would require asset-license details, exact source revision, human-authored change notes, test results, or prompts/tool roles in the handoff.

This is an early free project at https://game-commons-captain.thabiggdogg420.chatgpt.site/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=community&utm_campaign=games_never_die&utm_content=aigamedev_handoff. The homepage’s big mashups are AI-generated concept art, not playable games; there is no automatic game generator yet.
